_comment: Matcher weights for the `pursuit` profile -- the Pursuit AI-Native cohort: ~30 Builders, entry-level, AI-adjacent, all industries, NYC (CLAUDE.md 'What this is'). THIS FILE DESCRIBES A POPULATION, NOT A PERSON, and it is the first criteria file in this repo that does. config/criteria.json is one software engineer's job search; every number here was chosen against the cohort corpus instead, and where the two files disagree the disagreement is deliberate and is written down below. Imported by migrations/migrate_profiles.py --profile pursuit --criteria-file config/pursuit-criteria.json --persona-file config/pursuit-persona.json --bump --budget 0; thereafter profiles.criteria_json is authoritative and this file is the diffable record of where the numbers came from.
_scale: match_score = clamp(base + sum(deltas), 0, 100), match.py:73-273. A delta <= -100 (HARD_EXCLUDE_AT, match.py:60) short-circuits to 0 regardless of every other rule. Deltas are absolute points so they read directly against the 0-100 result and against MATCH_FLOOR = 40 (schema.py:206), below which match.py writes no row at all.
_unfitted: EVERY NUMBER IN THIS FILE IS UNFITTED, and there is currently nothing to fit it against. Task 29's human labels do not exist (HANDOFF.md:237-247 -- 07's tooling is built and produced zero labels by design) and job_events is empty, so both L0 and L2 of the three measurement layers are unavailable and L1 (fit_score) is this profile's own downstream output, which CLAUDE.md forbids evaluating on. config/criteria.json:106 says the same of the author's numbers, which at least had one calibration pass against existing job_scores rows; these have had none. CLAUDE.md: 'do not re-tune on a provisional number.' WHAT WOULD FIT THEM, in order of value: (1) task 29's Builder labels, which are the only non-circular signal that will ever exist for this population -- the master plan is explicit that outcome labels will never exist (MASTER-PLAN-pursuit.md:39-42), so Builder preference IS the ground truth; (2) job_events once the app has users; (3) nothing else. Do not tune these against fit_score.
_selection_note: THE WEIGHT SET WAS CHOSEN BY THE REPO OWNER from three simulated variants, on 2026-07-28, against the 863-row cohort corpus. Simulated outcome at these numbers: 145 of 863 clear MATCH_FLOOR (16.8%), 19 of the top 20 are entry-level x uses_ai_tools, and 51 of the 55 SHARED-FLOOR postings clear it. READ THAT THIRD FIGURE PRECISELY, because a looser reading of it is wrong: the 55 are the postings with an entry-level seniority (intern, new_grad or junior) AND ai_involvement = uses_ai_tools. LOCATION IS NOT ONE OF THE CONJUNCTS. Adding it -- entry x uses_ai_tools x NYC-or-remote -- gives 24 postings of which 23 clear the floor, a different and much smaller population. Location is deliberately left out of the definition because location is a PENALTY here and not a gate (see _location_comment: a non-NYC posting is demoted, never excluded), so conditioning the target population on it would measure the rule against itself. All three figures are reproduced offline by tests/test_match.py against evals/fixtures/pursuit-criteria-corpus.jsonl, the 863 rows frozen on 2026-07-28. That is a prediction recorded so a later edit can be checked against it: re-run before changing any number here, and if the counts have moved without an edit, the corpus moved and the counts are the finding.
_base_comment: 50, inherited unchanged from the placeholder this file replaces (migrations/migrate_pursuit_profile.py:198, PLACEHOLDER_CRITERIA). It is 15 above the author's 35 and that is a consequence of the archetype scale, not an independent decision: this profile's largest positive archetype is +14 against the author's +30, so a smaller spread needs a higher intercept to keep on-target postings clear of the floor. base 50 minus MATCH_FLOOR 40 leaves 10 points of headroom, which is one tolerated seniority notch (intern, -5) plus one missing field -- deliberately tight, because a cohort profile that admits everything is the placeholder's uniform ranking with extra steps.
_seniority_comment: The cohort is entry-level and that is the one thing about it that is not in dispute (MASTER-PLAN-pursuit.md:24, 'Target roles: Entry-level'). target is new_grad and junior. THE TASK FILE ASKED FOR THREE VALUES AND ONE OF THEM DOES NOT EXIST: 13-cohort-criteria-profile.md:39 specifies target ['entry','junior','new_grad'], but `entry` is in neither match.SENIORITY_ORDER (match.py:65-66) nor extract.SENIORITY (extract.py:205-206). match.py:152-154 filters targets through `if t in SENIORITY_ORDER`, so an `entry` target would be silently dropped from the distance fallback and would never be matched by an extracted value, because the extractor cannot emit it. Adding it to the vocabulary means a FACTS_VERSION bump and a full re-extraction of the corpus for a synonym of two values already present. It is deliberately absent; the task file carries a correction block.
_seniority_intern_comment: intern is TOLERATED at -5, not excluded. config/criteria.json:48 hard-excludes it, and that is right for a 5-YOE engineer and wrong here: paid apprenticeships, fellowships and internships are a legitimate entry path for career changers, Pursuit's own model includes embedded placements, and the cohort gate deliberately added \yintern(ship)?s?\y to its entry-level vocabulary because omitting it dropped every internship and new-grad programme (the gate was extracted from that migration into config/pursuit-relevance.json:10, _entry_level_note). -5 rather than 0 because an unpaid or student-only internship is a real mismatch for a career changer with rent, and the extractor cannot tell those apart; a small penalty ranks a genuine apprenticeship below a genuine junior role without removing it.
_seniority_penalties_comment: mid -25, senior -45. Both are set so the posting lands BELOW the floor on seniority alone unless something else carries it: base 50 - 45 = 5 for senior, and 50 - 25 = 25 for mid, against MATCH_FLOOR 40. A mid posting therefore needs +15 of archetype and AI signal to appear at all, which is the intended behaviour -- 'mid-level' in a posting written by a company that means it is not reachable, but 'mid' is also what the extractor returns for a great many postings that ask for two years and a pulse, and a hard exclude would delete those. senior at -45 is a de facto exclude that still leaves a paper trail in match_reasons instead of a 0.
_seniority_hard_exclude_comment: staff, principal, director, exec. These four are unambiguous in a title and are never a fit for an entry-level cohort, so they short-circuit to 0 (match.py:137-139). WHY new_grad-adjacent ERRORS ARE PRICED AND NOT EXCLUDED: seniority_level self-agrees 85.2% [77.6-90.6] on repeat extraction (n=115, deepseek-v4-flash at temperature 0, docs/ingestion_tests/README.md:128), so roughly one posting in seven is assigned a different level on a second pass. A hard exclude amplifies that 1-in-7 into a deleted posting; a penalty makes it cost points. The four excluded here are the levels where a slip is least likely -- 'Staff Engineer' and 'VP' are not subtle -- and the exclusion is additionally belt-and-braces, because this profile's relevance gate already drops \ysenior\y, \ystaff\y, \yprincipal\y and \ydirector\y from titles (config/pursuit-relevance.json:101 title_exclude, argued at :145). This block catches the ones whose TITLE is clean and whose BODY asks for ten years. NOTE THE CITATION, because this is the one the task file (13-cohort-criteria-profile.md:105-107) asks to be corrected rather than inherited: config/criteria.json's _hard_exclude_comment justified the same design with a pair of self-agreement figures from tools/compare-extract.py that task 06 measured and could not reproduce -- both were optimistic, and the correction landed in that file on 2026-07-28 ('FIGURES CORRECTED 2026-07-28 (task 06)', config/criteria.json:43). The superseded numbers are DELIBERATELY NOT QUOTED HERE, in either direction: a new file repeating a dead figure to say it is dead is how a dead figure survives. The live measurements are the n=115 ones above and in docs/ingestion_tests/README.md:126-132; tests/test_match.py asserts this file does not carry the old pair.
_seniority_unknown_comment: -2, and set deliberately rather than inheriting the author's -4 (config/criteria.json:50), per 13-cohort-criteria-profile.md:44-46. seniority_level is the second-least-stable field match.py scores and is NULL on exactly 1 of 5,321 rows today only because extract.normalize() used to substitute a sentinel; task 11 made it preserve None, so the true absence rate on the messy, all-industry, non-ATS sources Phase 3 is aimed at is unknown and will not be small. An unknown level on a hospital's careers page is a property of the page, not evidence about the role. -2 is one notch of noise, enough that 'we could not tell' ranks below 'we could tell and it was on target' without suppressing the employers this whole retarget exists to surface.
_seniority_penalty_per_level_comment: 14, the safety net config/criteria.json:44 documents. It is inert TODAY -- all nine values of SENIORITY_ORDER are named above, three in target, three in tolerate, four in hard_exclude -- and it exists so that the next level added to the vocabulary is never silently free, which is exactly the defect `staff` had in the author's profile until 2026-07-27. 14 is set so the fallback is roughly consistent with the named penalties: mid is one level above junior and priced -25, senior is two above and priced -45, so a per-level rate of ~14-22 interpolates them; 14 is the conservative end.
_years_experience_comment: max_required 2. A Builder finishing a 5-month program has no professional years in this field, and 13-cohort-criteria-profile.md:69-73 asks for postings demanding more than ~2 years to be penalised steeply. over_penalty_per_year 10 with a cap of 30 means a 3-year ask costs 10, a 5-year ask costs 30, and everything beyond 5 costs the same 30 -- the cap is there because the difference between 'wants 8 years' and 'wants 15 years' is not a difference this cohort can act on, and an uncapped penalty would let one badly-parsed number dominate the ranking. 50 - 30 = 20 against a floor of 40, so a posting asking 5+ years needs 20 points of other signal to survive, which is more than any single archetype here is worth.
_years_experience_no_prior_domain_commen: PRIOR-DOMAIN EXPERIENCE IS DELIBERATELY NOT MODELLED HERE, per 13-cohort-criteria-profile.md:75-79. A Builder may be fifteen years senior in nursing and entry-level in AI. years_experience_min describes what the POSTING demands, not what the person has, and there is no scalar in this file that can represent 'these fifteen years transfer'. That story belongs in gap_bridging_angle, which is the narrative tier's job and the thing LLMs are actually good at. Encoding it as a weight is how you get a config nobody can reason about.
_years_experience_missing_note: years_experience_min is NULL on 52.9% of job_facts rows (config/criteria.json:108, measured 2026-07-28), by far the most-missing scored field, so this block is silent on more than half the corpus and unknown_penalty.years_experience_min below is what actually fires there. Read the two together.
_ai_involvement_comment: THE INVERSION IS THE POINT, AND IT IS THE SINGLE LINE IN THIS FILE MOST LIKELY TO BE 'CORRECTED' BY SOMEONE READING config/criteria.json BESIDE IT. uses_ai_tools is 20 and builds_llm_features is 8 -- the opposite ordering to the author's profile, which prices builds_llm_features 12 against uses_ai_tools 6 (config/criteria.json:81-86), in this same repo, two files apart. Both are correct for their profile. The author is five months into an agent/LLM integration program and wants to BUILD the features; the cohort's entire targeting mechanism is roles that USE AI tools -- MASTER-PLAN-pursuit.md:24 defines the target as 'Entry-level, AI-adjacent (ai_involvement = uses_ai_tools), all industries', and 13-cohort-criteria-profile.md:59-61 says it in as many words. A posting that wants someone to run Zapier flows and prompt ChatGPT well is reachable by a Builder on graduation day; a posting that wants someone to ship LLM features into a production codebase mostly is not, which is why builds_llm_features stays POSITIVE (it is a genuine stretch role, not a wrong one) but at 8 rather than 20. DO NOT SWAP THESE TO MATCH THE AUTHOR'S FILE. WHY 20 IS THE LARGEST SINGLE POSITIVE IN THIS FILE, larger than any archetype: it is also the most reliable. ai_involvement self-agrees 94.8% [89.1-97.6] on repeat extraction against role_archetype's 84.3% [76.6-89.9] (n=115, docs/ingestion_tests/README.md:126-129), so it is both the feature that defines the target and the feature the extractor is best at. none -30 rather than 0 (the author's value) because a posting with no AI involvement at all is not AI-adjacent, which is half the definition of the shared floor. core_ml_research -60 transfers from the author's file unchanged and for a stronger reason: research roles are out of reach for a career changer with no graduate degree, and the cohort has no degree requirement by design.
_archetypes_comment: All 26 values of extract.ARCHETYPE (extract.py:247-259) are priced. THE COMPLETENESS IS LOAD-BEARING, not tidiness: match.py:180-191 sends any value this map does not name down the `archetype:{v}:unpriced` path and charges it unknown_penalty.role_archetype, so an omission is not a zero -- it is a penalty applied to a value someone thought they were leaving neutral. Check the count against extract.ARCHETYPE after any change to that tuple.
_archetypes_ordering_comment: The scale runs 14 down to -45 and is compressed on purpose. The author's file spans +30 to -55 because that profile knows what it wants; this one does not, and MASTER-PLAN-pursuit.md:41-42 is explicit that it cannot: 'There is no single target role. Builders are at different stages with a hands-off curriculum. The shared floor -- entry-level, AI-adjacent, NYC, no degree required -- is well-defined. Anything narrower is invented.' A 14-point spread lets archetype order the list without letting it decide admission; seniority, ai_involvement and location decide admission. THE OPS VALUES LEAD: support_ops and implementation_analyst at 14, then admin_ops, marketing_ops and ai_operations at 12. These are the roles where an entry-level person who is fluent with AI tools is immediately more valuable than the incumbent, and they are the roles the author's profile prices at -10 to -35 -- the inversion the archetype superset was built to make possible (config/criteria.json:11: 'a software profile prices the ops values at or below zero, the cohort profile (task 13) does the reverse').
_archetypes_ai_operations_comment: ai_operations is 12 -- LEVEL WITH THE OTHER OPS VALUES AND DELIBERATELY NOT ABOVE THEM, which is the one judgement in this block most likely to look like an error. It is the archetype the whole retarget is named after and it is 17 postings, 2.0% of the 863-row cohort corpus. 11 of its 14 employers are tech companies -- Brex, Harvey, Coinbase, Databricks, Figma, Samsara, Vanta (HANDOFF.md:113-119) -- so the value is being found where the pipeline was already strong, not in the all-industries NYC market this retarget is aimed at. Meanwhile support_ops is 82 rows, 60% of the ops mass and nearly 5x ai_operations (HANDOFF.md:121-126). Weighting the archetype the project is named after above the one the corpus actually contains would price the INTENTION rather than the EVIDENCE, and it would concentrate the top of the list on fourteen tech employers. It is not priced DOWN either -- it is a genuine target when it appears. REJECTED: 18-20, which was the first draft and was reversed on the employer-spread finding. Re-check this the moment Phase 3 sourcing lands non-tech employers; the number is low because the corpus is, not because the role is wrong.
_archetypes_other_comment: other is 0, NOT NEGATIVE, and this is the most consequential single decision in the file. `other` is 268 of the 863 cohort rows -- 31.1% -- and 44.0% of first-time extractions, against 4.6% on rows that already had v2 facts (docs/facts-v3-diff.md:410-422). Expanding the vocabulary from 12 values to 26 was followed by `other` roughly QUADRUPLING as a share, because the 26 were derived from a tech-heavy corpus and 44% of the actual cohort corpus -- entry-level, all-industry, NYC -- is unnamed by them. 14 of the 55 postings that meet the shared floor in full sit at `other`. Penalising it would suppress a quarter of the addressable set on the basis that a vocabulary known to fail on new postings failed on them, which is measuring the extractor and calling it a property of the job. 0 is also exactly the treatment `other` gets in the author's file (config/criteria.json:39) and it means the same thing there: no information, no verdict. THE CORRECT FIX IS NOT A WEIGHT. It is re-deriving the vocabulary against the corpus that now exists (docs/role-track-derivation.md, and the O*NET/SOC escape hatch recorded at extract.py:238-246). Until then, do not make this number negative to 'clean up' the list; you would be deleting the roles nobody has named yet.
_archetypes_software_comment: THE SOFTWARE VALUES ARE ZERO, NOT NEGATIVE -- frontend, fullstack, backend, mobile, devops, security, infrastructure_compute, hardware_embedded. 13-cohort-criteria-profile.md:63-67 asks for exactly this: 'a Builder who does have some technical aptitude should not be actively steered away from a junior developer posting.' Builders come from a program that teaches building; some will be strong enough for a junior developer role and the profile must not delete those postings. 0 means the posting is admitted or not on its OTHER signals -- entry-level seniority, AI involvement, location -- which is the right test. hardware_embedded and security are 0 rather than negative for the weaker reason that they are simply rare here and a negative number on a rare value is a guess with no corpus behind it.
_archetypes_bridge_comment: solutions 10, it_internal 10, business_systems 10, program_management 8, forward_deployed 8, ai_integration 6. These are the bridge roles -- customer-facing or internal-systems work with a technical edge -- and they are the second tier because they are genuinely reachable but usually want some prior context. it_internal and business_systems are notable inversions of the author's file, which prices them -20 and -15 (config/criteria.json:29-31): internal helpdesk and Salesforce/Workday configuration are far from a 5-YOE production engineer and close to an entry-level career changer who is fluent with AI tools. ai_integration is the LOWEST of this tier at 6 despite being the most AI-shaped name in the vocabulary, because it is the author's +26 and it means shipping LLM features in a production codebase -- the same reasoning as builds_llm_features above.
_archetypes_technical_adjacent_comment: data 4, pm 4, qa_test 4, developer_relations 4. Adjacent, entry paths exist, but all four commonly carry a requirement the cohort cannot meet on graduation -- an analytics stack for data, product experience for pm, a public track record for developer_relations. 4 is 'do not bury this' rather than 'seek this out'. NOTE ONE POISONED VALUE: three postings in the corpus carry scraped browser DOM as their description_text and one of them (Taboola, Product Analyst, job ff9f9d9f9643e185af0f48ca) was extracted from a scraped ChatGPT web UI into a confident role_archetype = 'data' (HANDOFF.md:403-417). That is an ingest defect, not a pricing one, and the low value here is not a response to it -- but anyone tuning `data` should know one of its rows is not a job.
_archetypes_negative_comment: Only two values are negative. engineering_management -20: a management role is a level mismatch before it is a domain one, and 50 - 20 = 30 puts it below the floor without a hard exclude, which is right because 'Engineering Manager' is occasionally an extraction slip on a senior IC title. ml_research -45: the cohort has no degree requirement by design (MASTER-PLAN-pursuit.md:24, and flags.advanced_degree_required below), and research roles require exactly the graduate credential the population does not have. -45 and not -100: a hard exclude here would amplify role_archetype's 15.7% self-disagreement rate into deleted postings, and the genuinely disqualifying version of this is already caught by flags.ml_research_required at -100, which is a direct extracted answer rather than an inferred category. REJECTED: negative values for pm, program_management and admin_ops, all of which the author's file prices at -28 to -35. Every one of those is a plausible destination for a career changer with strong AI-tool fluency, and this profile has no business ruling them out.
_tech_comment: EMPTY, AND EMPTY IS THE DECISION. cap 0 and no boosts, so the tech rule (match.py:220-231) contributes nothing to this profile's ranking. The author's file boosts thirteen terms up to a cap of 26 because a stack list is evidence about a software engineer's fit. It is evidence about nothing here: the cohort spans all industries, has no shared stack, and MASTER-PLAN-pursuit.md:41-42 forbids inventing a target narrower than the shared floor -- a boost list IS such an invention, and it would quietly re-sort an all-industries list towards the software postings that happen to name Python. THE CAP IS 0 RATHER THAN THE KEY BEING ABSENT so that a future editor adding a boost has to also raise the cap, and cannot turn this rule on by accident. tech_stack is also the least stable field the extractor produces -- 70.4% exact, 85.4% Jaccard (docs/ingestion_tests/README.md:130) -- which is a second, independent reason not to rank on it. Absence of a stack is never penalised either: unknown_penalty.tech_stack below is 0, for the same reason.
_location_comment: NYC and remote both accepted; the cohort is a New York City cohort (MASTER-PLAN-pursuit.md:24) and remote is kept beside it because a remote posting is reachable from NYC. Reads jobs.location_is_nyc / location_is_remote, which lib.text computes at ingest for free, falling back to job_facts.remote_policy only to tell 'onsite somewhere else' (a real no, -25) from 'we could not classify this' (a data gap, -15). THE ASYMMETRY IS THE WHOLE RULE: 50 - 15 = 35 puts an unclassifiable location just below the floor, recoverable by one good archetype or a uses_ai_tools, while 50 - 25 = 25 puts a confirmed onsite-elsewhere posting beyond reach of anything except uses_ai_tools plus an ops archetype. Neither is a hard exclude because a mis-parsed location would then delete a posting outright, and location parsing is exactly the thing the messy Phase 3 sources are worst at. 444 of the 876 rows the cohort gate admits (50.7%) are NYC-or-remote (config/pursuit-relevance.json:177, _location_note), so this rule fires on roughly half the corpus and its magnitudes matter more here than in the author's file. FILTER HERE, NOT AT INGEST: 13-cohort-criteria-profile.md:93-95 and the master plan both require non-NYC rows to stop being discarded upstream -- storage is free, the fetch already happened, and geographic expansion should be a config edit rather than a re-crawl.
_flags_comment: gap_friendly_language 10 transfers from the author's file at its exact value and means something broader here: the author's reentry_growth bucket is about one 2.5-year break, while this cohort is career changers as a population, so a posting that says 'no experience required', 'we will train' or 'non-traditional backgrounds welcome' is signalling that the single largest barrier this population faces is absent. It is the highest-value flag in the file relative to how cheap it is to detect -- gap_friendly_language self-agrees 100% [96.8-100] on repeat extraction (docs/ingestion_tests/README.md:132). customer_facing 8: ops, support and implementation work is customer-facing by nature, so this correlates with the archetypes priced highest above, and it is one of the more reliable extracted booleans at 95.7% [90.2-98.1]. ADVANCED_DEGREE_REQUIRED -45 IS THE SHARED FLOOR'S FOURTH TERM. 'No degree required' is not a preference of this population, it is a defining constraint (MASTER-PLAN-pursuit.md:41-42), and it transfers from the author's file at -45 unchanged because the magnitude was right for a different reason and is right for this one. 50 - 45 = 5: below the floor, but not a 0, because the extractor sometimes reads 'BS/BA or equivalent experience' as a requirement. ml_research_required -100 is a hard exclude (HARD_EXCLUDE_AT, match.py:60) and short-circuits the score to 0. It is the one hard exclude in this file that is not about seniority, and it is safe to make absolute because the field self-agrees 100% [96.8-100] -- unlike role_archetype's ml_research, which is an inferred category and is therefore priced at -45 instead.
_unknown_penalty_comment: What a field costs when the extractor could not answer it (match.py:96-132, keyed by job_facts COLUMN NAME). CONSERVATIVE ON PURPOSE, AND MORE CONSERVATIVE THAN THE AUTHOR'S FILE ON EVERY KEY THAT DIFFERS. 13-cohort-criteria-profile.md:81-86 gives the reason and it is the most important sentence in that section: the messy sources arriving in Phase 3 will produce many unknowns, and an aggressive missingness penalty would systematically suppress exactly the non-tech employers this refactor exists to surface. A hospital's careers page that does not state a seniority level is not a worse job than a Greenhouse posting that does; it is a worse-formatted page. Every number here is a fraction of its own rule's on-target value: role_archetype -3 against a +14 maximum, ai_involvement -3 against +20, advanced_degree_required -3 and ml_research_required -4 against -45 and -100. Compare config/criteria.json:111-121, which prices the same four at -6, -4, -6 and -8 -- roughly double, for a profile whose corpus is clean ATS postings.
_unknown_penalty_zeroes_comment: FOUR ZEROES, ALL DELIBERATE. tech_stack 0: this profile has no tech boosts at all (see _tech_comment), so charging for a missing stack would be charging for the absence of something that is worth nothing when present. remote_policy 0: its absence is ALREADY charged, once, by location.neither_penalty -- match.py:233-258 treats 'we could not classify this' as location:unmatched and the _location_comment says so -- and any nonzero value here is a SECOND charge for the same absence. match.py emits a separate remote:missing reason regardless, so if someone does set it the double charge is visible in match_reasons rather than buried. gap_friendly_language 0 and customer_facing 0: both are bonuses, and absence of a bonus is already its own cost. Charging for a missing bonus converts a bonus into a requirement, which for gap_friendly_language would be actively perverse -- it would penalise every employer who simply did not write a diversity paragraph.
_unknown_penalty_rates_note: READ THE RATE BEFORE CHANGING A MAGNITUDE. years_experience_min is NULL on 52.9% of job_facts rows and role_archetype, ai_involvement and the booleans were NULL on ZERO rows as of 2026-07-28 -- but that was an artefact of extract.normalize() substituting sentinels, which task 11 removed (config/criteria.json:108). These penalties therefore start firing at their true, unmeasured absence rates as v3 extraction spreads, and the first honest measurement of those rates should come before anyone raises a number here. A -N on a field that turns out to be NULL on half the corpus is a corpus-wide re-ranking, not a rounding.
